questions.topic: Selecting and Ordering Retrieved Context
questions.question: Why should overlapping retrieved chunks be deduplicated before prompt assembly?
options: Repeated passages consume budget and can displace evidence from another source
Repeated passages always receive different tenant labels from the vector index
Repeated passages prevent the reranker from assigning any score to the query
Repeated passages make every source identifier impossible to map to a document

questions.topic: Selecting and Ordering Retrieved Context
questions.question: What tradeoff does maximal marginal relevance make?
options: Citation accuracy against generation speed
Query relevance against redundancy with selected items
Metadata completeness against index compression
Prompt length against answer output length

questions.topic: Selecting and Ordering Retrieved Context
questions.question: A query compares retail and wholesale policies, but the top results all repeat retail details. Which assembly change best improves coverage?
options: Set MMR to pure relevance so similar retail chunks dominate selection
Place every retail chunk in the middle and omit wholesale evidence
Use an MMR diversity penalty so a wholesale chunk can enter the context
Remove source labels so the model can blend both policies without attribution

questions.topic: Selecting and Ordering Retrieved Context
questions.question: How should several chunks from the same document usually be ordered?
options: Randomly between unrelated sources to maximize position variance
Strictly by chunk length from shortest to longest
In descending source identifier regardless of document sequence
Adjacently in original document order to preserve coherence

questions.topic: Selecting and Ordering Retrieved Context
questions.question: When is lost-in-the-middle placement most operationally important?
options: In long assemblies where important evidence can be buried among many chunks
In a three-chunk prompt where deterministic order dominates small position effects
Before retrieval, when no candidates or context positions exist yet
Only when all chunks are exact duplicates with identical source positions

questions.topic: Selecting and Ordering Retrieved Context
questions.question: What does setting lambda to 1 in the stated MMR objective do?
options: It selects only candidates least similar to the query
It removes the diversity penalty and restores pure relevance selection
It gives redundancy twice the weight of query similarity
It forces the first and last candidates to use the same source

questions.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources
questions.question: What must assembly provide so generated citation markers can be resolved?
options: An unlabeled block containing all retrieved text in score order
A random label regenerated independently during final rendering
Stable source labels mapped to documents, chunks, and offsets
Only a list of document titles without corresponding chunk text

questions.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources
questions.question: What does exact quote verification prove?
options: The quoted span logically entails every generated claim
The source document is globally trustworthy and current
The answer contains no unsupported connective language
The quoted text exists in the source assigned by the citation

questions.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources
questions.question: A model emits a plausible quotation that does not occur in its cited chunk. What should a span-grounded pipeline do?
options: Reject or regenerate it after deterministic matching fails
Accept it because the source label has a valid numeric format
Move it to another source without checking that source text
Remove quotation marks and treat it as mechanically verified

questions.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources
questions.question: Why are sentence-level citations generally preferable to answer-level source lists?
options: They eliminate the need to include source text in the prompt
They connect individual claims to evidence that a user can verify
They prove automatically that each cited passage entails its claim
They allow labels to change after generation without maintaining a map

questions.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources
questions.question: Which remaining check is needed after a quoted span has been matched exactly?
options: Whether the label is the longest identifier in the assembled prompt
Whether the chunk was ranked by BM25 rather than dense retrieval
Whether the matched span actually supports the generated claim
Whether every word in the answer has a separate source marker

questions.topic: Citation-Grounded Extraction: Attributing Spans to Sources
questions.question: The retrieved sources genuinely lack the requested fact. What behavior should a grounded system permit?
options: Invent the fact and attach the label of the highest-ranked chunk
Cite every retrieved source so the unsupported claim appears well grounded
Suppress the missing evidence and answer from model memory without disclosure
Refuse or state that the provided sources do not support an answer

questions.topic: Metadata Filters in Context Assembly
questions.question: What can metadata filtering guarantee that semantic similarity cannot?
options: That a result belongs to the required tenant, date, type, or status
That every returned chunk has the highest possible cosine similarity
That a language model will never misinterpret a supporting passage
That all documents have complete metadata for every optional field

questions.topic: Metadata Filters in Context Assembly
questions.question: What is the main difference between pre-filtering and post-filtering?
options: Pre-filtering discards results after generation; post-filtering changes the source
Pre-filtering constrains search candidates; post-filtering discards retrieved hits
Pre-filtering applies only inferred years; post-filtering applies only tenant security
Pre-filtering removes metadata; post-filtering creates metadata from model output

questions.topic: Metadata Filters in Context Assembly
questions.question: Eight of ten retrieved hits fail a post-filter, leaving only two chunks for a top-10 request. What is the direct mitigation when pre-filtering is unavailable?
options: Fetch fewer than ten candidates so fewer results can fail
Disable the filter and expose every disallowed result to the prompt
Overfetch according to the expected pass rate to obtain enough survivors
Duplicate the two survivors until the prompt contains ten chunks

questions.topic: Metadata Filters in Context Assembly
questions.question: An inferred year makes search empty, but the tenant constraint is security-critical. How should a relaxation ladder respond?
options: Drop the tenant first because it is a system default
Drop all constraints without telling the user
Keep the wrong year and fabricate matching evidence
Relax the inferred year while preserving the tenant constraint

questions.topic: Metadata Filters in Context Assembly
questions.question: Why must tenant filtering be enforced as an unconditional system constraint?
options: A prompt or inferred parser is not a reliable authorization boundary
Tenant metadata always improves cosine similarity for every query
Post-filtering guarantees enough allowed hits without overfetching
Users should be able to relax tenant filters when results are sparse

questions.topic: Metadata Filters in Context Assembly
questions.question: What should be checked before enforcing a filter over an optional metadata field?
options: Whether the field name is longer than each stored chunk identifier
Whether metadata coverage is high enough to avoid silently excluding unlabeled documents
Whether the reranker score can be converted directly into a tenant identifier
Whether all inferred constraints are retained even after an empty result

questions.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume
questions.question: What is relevance density?
options: The number of retrieved documents divided by the corpus size
The output token reserve divided by the system prompt size
The useful context tokens divided by total context tokens
The reranker latency divided by the number of candidate scores

questions.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume
questions.question: Why is the calculated context allocation a ceiling rather than a target?
options: Every unused token automatically reduces the model's maximum answer length
A model cannot process a prompt unless every available token is filled
Retrieved chunks have no cost or latency once the context window is known
Low-relevance padding can add distraction, latency, and cost while reducing quality

questions.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume
questions.question: An 8,000-token window reserves 600 for system text, 400 for history, 100 for the question, and 1,500 for output. What is the context ceiling?
options: 5,400 tokens
5,900 tokens
6,500 tokens
7,900 tokens

questions.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume
questions.question: Reranker scores are 0.92, 0.88, 0.85, 0.41, and 0.39. What does a dynamic-k policy likely do?
options: Pad to the maximum chunk count regardless of the score collapse
Admit the first three and stop before the low-score distractors
Discard the first three because high scores consume more tokens
Duplicate the fourth and fifth chunks to stabilize context length

questions.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume
questions.question: Strong candidates exceed the token budget. Which action most directly raises relevance density?
options: Add lower-ranked context until every window position is occupied
Increase answer reserve while retaining all overlapping chunk text
Merge overlaps and extract the query-relevant spans from long chunks
Remove source metadata and repeat each candidate in several positions

questions.topic: Context Window Budgeting: Relevance Density over Volume
questions.question: Which query type most justifies a generous context budget?
options: A factoid lookup answered by one short authoritative span
A navigational request for one known document title
A lookup whose top reranker score is separated by a large margin
A multi-document synthesis whose answer requires evidence across sources
